plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, overbidding risks paying more than my value warrants, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit no matter the strategies of Betty and Charles, since the mechanism is incentive-compatible. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit because you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning when the item isn't worth it; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $35.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true even with the mutual knowledge of rationality - since payment equals the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $6.
